extracted.intended_audience: creative professionals, in-house teams, agency-side creatives, students and aspiring creatives
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the qualities and organisational values D&AD presents as the benchmark for award-winning work, covering both professional (Pencil) and student/New Blood categories and the benefits of winning. Useful for entrants deciding whether to enter and understanding what the awards value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative bravery
rubrics_metrics.description: The benchmark for creative bravery — work that moves culture and challenges the creative industries to do better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D&AD positions its awards as recognising work that 'moves culture' and pushes the craft forward; entries should challenge norms and demonstrate courageous, culture-shifting ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour and integrity (D&AD Pencil for professionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For professionals – the industry benchmark for commercial creativity, the D&AD Pencil stands for rigour and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional entries are expected to demonstrate high standards of craft and commercial relevance; the Pencil is described as a recognition of rigour and integrity in work produced for the market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassuringly difficult / high standard
rubrics_metrics.description: We famously set the bar high, so that your award means something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should expect tough judging and aim for excellence — the organisation emphasises that difficulty of award standards ensures that winning is meaningful rather than easy-to-obtain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Entered by almost 90 countries, a win marks your position on the global stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that has international relevance, reach or comparability is positioned as being rewarded; winning signals global standing and should reflect standards that travel across markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-defining impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A Pencil earns you lasting respect from employers and your peers. It can help swing an interview, a pitch, and even the odd invite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should be of a quality and distinction likely to influence career opportunities and peer recognition — D&AD frames awards as materially beneficial to entrants' careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative connecting / community benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners join the trusted D&AD community for support and advice, and to make work that pushes our craft forwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the award itself, successful work should demonstrate potential to connect creators and contribute to the broader creative community; networking and mentorship benefits are highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not-for-profit / reinvestment into education
rubrics_metrics.description: Not for profit — Enter and support future generations. All our surplus is reinvested into education and development programmes such as Shift and New Blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards are framed as supporting education and development; entrants are implicitly encouraged to view participation as contributing to community and future talent development rather than a purely commercial endeavour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting: Professional vs New Blood categories
rubrics_metrics.description: D&AD Awards — For professionals; New Blood Awards — for students and starters. 'Launch your career in advertising and design with an award for students, graduates and aspiring creatives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must select the appropriate category (professional Pencil for industry work; New Blood for students/graduates/starters). New Blood is explicitly pitched as career-launching and aimed at emerging creatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of judging ('Judged by the best')
rubrics_metrics.description: Judged by the best, a Pencil is a recognition, a career shifter, and a green-eyed provoking inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emphasis on senior/high-calibre judges implies that entries should meet expectations of industry leaders; credibility of judging is presented as part of the award's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of cultural or commercial relevance ('something that matters')
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you’re in-house, agency-side, or solo creator, it is proof you’ve made something that matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants are encouraged to demonstrate that their work has tangible cultural or commercial significance — not just craft for craft's sake but work with meaningful impact or purpose.
